segments.text: I woke up late with a winner in my blood
Curtain shut tight, every noon looked like mud
Coffee on the counter, cold as a stop-dub clock
I was dragging my name down the block
Doctor held a paper under white forest and rain
Said you ain't lazy man, you've been running on pain
I laughed through my teeth, then I stared at the floor
Like somebody had finally unlocked the door
Little gold tablet, little beam in my hand
I didn't know the sun could fit in a plan

i was praying to the ceiling with a dead phone in my chest then the daylight found my number
and it told me i could rest vitamin d i ain't saying you're the lord but you showed up like a

fog when i'd speak tony's bones are turning to dust that's what i used to say tony's balls are
turning to dust better hide on the way i made a joke because the truth had a heavyweight swing

I don't need to explain every bright thing I see
